column3: The Hebrew names thick darkness; BSB says thick cloud.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the whole assembly of Israel twice and explicitly says the king turned his face; BSB condenses both.
The Hebrew uses plural hands and narrates speaking before fulfillment; BSB has singular hand and puts fulfillment first.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not include a separate now.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the son coming from David’s loins; BSB uses your own offspring.
The Hebrew repeats the root for establishing and arising and says the LORD spoke; BSB uses fulfilled, succeeded, and promised.
The Hebrew says I placed the ark there, rather than providing a place for it.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed here and specifically mentions his palms; BSB supplies Solomon.
The Hebrew explicitly mentions kneeling on his knees and spreading his palms; BSB condenses these.
The Hebrew coordinates covenant and loyalty; BSB describes a covenant of loving devotion.
The Hebrew says what You spoke and repeats speaking with the mouth; BSB begins with promise.
The Hebrew uses the image of a man being cut off and calls the descendants sons.
The Hebrew asks that Your word be confirmed, without a separate word for promised.
The Hebrew calls the building this house; BSB uses this temple.
The Hebrew describes turning toward the prayer; BSB says regard it.
The Hebrew calls the building this house; BSB uses this temple.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes an oath coming before the altar in this house; BSB makes the man come to take an oath in this temple.
The Hebrew pictures returning the guilty man’s way onto his head; BSB paraphrases this as what he has done.
The Hebrew leaves the destination of returning unstated and calls the building this house; BSB supplies to You and uses temple.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the sinning subject unnamed; BSB specifies Your people.
The Hebrew calls the land Your land, which You gave; BSB says the land that You gave.
The Hebrew pictures the siege in the land of its gates; BSB expresses cities.
The Hebrew includes any individual person as well as all Israel and mentions each person’s plague and pain; BSB focuses on Israel and uses afflictions.
The Hebrew uses singular heart in the final clause; BSB uses hearts.
